content.text:
I fixed the bug. When `v-for` loops over a `shallowReactive` array, it now hands you each item as it is, without making it deeply reactive. That means `item.aaa` stays a ref, so the template prints `object`, the same as accessing `shallowReactiveArray[0].aaa` directly.

**Cause:** `renderList` in `packages/runtime-core/src/helpers/renderList.ts` ran `toReactive()` on the items of any reactive array. It didn't check whether the array was shallow. A deep reactive wrapper unwraps refs, so `item.aaa` became the string `'aaa1'`.

**Fix:** items are now wrapped only when the array is not shallow (checked with `isShallow`). Deep `reactive` arrays behave as before.

The existing `renderList` tests pass (7/7). I didn't add a test for this exact case and didn't run the issue's reproduction. The editor shows type errors in that file: it can't find `@vue/reactivity`, `@vue/shared` and `__DEV__`. Those are about how the editor resolves the workspace packages, not the change itself. The tests compile and run fine.
